passage:
Every Thursday after school, older students helped younger students with homework in the library.
At first, the older students thought they would simply give answers. But the teacher told them, "Helping is not doing the work for someone. Helping is asking the right questions."
This was harder than expected. When a younger student could not solve a math problem, the helper had to explain steps patiently.
One older student said he understood math better after teaching it.
The program helped both sides. Younger students got support. Older students learned patience and clearer thinking.
The library became a place where knowledge moved in two directions, not just from older to younger.
